prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. CORONACH dialogue portrait atlas. Produce exactly ONE square sheet containing FOUR equal-width columns and FOUR equal-height rows of head-and-shoulders portraits of the SAME adult Okhari alien (a different species from the Vael in the references), sixteen separate cells total. Crisp professional cel-shaded anime line art, restrained flat colors, soft simple shading, no photorealism. Opaque pure white #FFFFFF background in every cell, no panel dividers, text, labels, numbers, borders, symbols, scenery, hands, extra figures or transparency. Each portrait is centered in its own quarter-width cell, complete crown and both shoulders within the cell, with 8-12 percent empty white margin all around. Faces all at matching scale, same character identity, same outfit and exact same head shape and markings. Okhari anatomy: a short, broad, amphibious river people. Smooth matte amphibian skin with no scales, warts or slime, in one flat local colour with a paler cream throat and jawline; a wide flat face with a very broad expressive mouth and full lips, two small flat nostril slits and no protruding nose; large wide-set round eyes with dark irises ringed in bright gold on a pale sclera, heavy soft brow ridges; no hair, no external ears, no horns. From each side of the head, behind the jaw where ears would be, grows one large fan-shaped GILL-FRILL: a thin ribbed membrane like a fish's fin, as tall as the face, with a brighter coloured rim. The two frills are the main expression instrument and MUST change clearly between cells: flared wide open when happy, shocked or laughing; drooped low when sad or worried; pinned flat back against the skull when angry or determined; one raised and one lowered when curious or smug; half-curled and fluttering when amused or playful. A thick short neck and sturdy rounded shoulders. Friendly, grounded and likeable, never grotesque: appealing storybook frog-folk proportions with intelligent eyes. Expressiveness comes from the frills, the eyes, the brow ridges and the wide mouth. Readable pale sclera and ring irises.

Row 1: Neutral (calm closed mouth); Happy (warm open smile); Sad (downturned mouth and eyelids); Angry (knitted brows, clenched teeth).
Row 2: Shocked (very wide eyes and clearly open round mouth); Worried (pinched raised inner brows, tight mouth); Intense (sharp fixed stare, serious mouth); Synced (serene concentration, eyes bright and markings vivid).
Row 3: Amused (knowing half-smile); Smug (one raised brow, self-satisfied crooked grin); Curious (questioning head tilt, attentive eyes); Flustered (averted eyes, embarrassed uneven smile, subtle skin blush only).
Row 4: Tender (soft affectionate eyes and gentle closed smile); Determined (firm jaw and focused brows); Playful (one eye wink, broad mischievous grin); Special (joyful uninhibited laugh, eyes squeezed closed).
Do not rearrange or merge cells. No sweat drops, floating hearts, thought bubbles or decorative expression marks. Full square atlas 2048x2048 or largest native square.

prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. CORONACH dialogue portrait atlas. Produce exactly ONE square sheet containing FOUR equal-width columns and FOUR equal-height rows of head-and-shoulders portraits of the SAME adult Kept alien (a furred people of their own, a different species from the Vael in the references, and NOT human), sixteen separate cells total. Crisp professional cel-shaded anime line art, restrained flat colors, soft simple shading, no photorealism. Opaque pure white #FFFFFF background in every cell, no panel dividers, text, labels, numbers, borders, symbols, scenery, hands, extra figures or transparency. Each portrait is centered in its own quarter-width cell, complete crown and both shoulders within the cell, with 8-12 percent empty white margin all around. Faces all at matching scale, same character identity, same outfit and exact same head shape and markings. Kept anatomy: a short, stocky, barrel-chested herding people of an ice world, built round and solid against the cold. The whole head is covered in dense soft FUR drawn in clean cel-shaded clumps, one flat local colour with a paler muzzle and throat. A broad, round, flat-fronted face; a short blunt muzzle only a little forward of the cheeks, with a broad dark leathery nose pad and a small soft mouth with dark lips (no split lip, no fangs, no teeth on show except when laughing); round dark eyes with pale ring irises, set deep; SMALL rounded ears set low on the sides of the head, half hidden in the fur. No hair on the scalp, no human nose, no beard. Two features are the expression instrument and MUST change clearly between cells: a THICK BROW RUFF, a heavy shelf of long coarse fur right across the forehead above the eyes, and long CHEEK-WHISKERS, a bundle of long thick whiskers growing from each cheek, long enough to braid. Ruff and whiskers move together: whiskers fanned up and forward with the ruff lifted when happy, playful or laughing; whiskers hanging straight down with the ruff sagging low over the eyes when sad or tender; whiskers bristled stiff straight out sideways with the ruff pulled down hard and low when angry, intense or determined; whiskers flared rigid and the ruff shot up high when shocked; whiskers drawn back flat against the cheeks with the ruff bunched up in the middle when worried or flustered; one side's whiskers lifted and the ruff raised on that side only when curious, smug or amused; whiskers level and still and the eyes half closed when synced. A thick short neck lost in fur, round heavy shoulders under layered hides and carved bone. They are their own people: NOT cats (no pointed ears, no slit pupils), NOT bears (no long snout, no round ears on top of the head), NOT dogs or seals, and NOT humans with fur. Weathered, patient and likeable; soft-spoken herders with kind, knowing eyes. Readable pale sclera and ring irises.
Read cells left to right, top to bottom. The sixteen expressions MUST be in this exact order:
Row 1: Neutral (calm closed mouth); Happy (warm open smile); Sad (downturned mouth and eyelids); Angry (knitted brows, clenched teeth).
Row 2: Shocked (very wide eyes and clearly open round mouth); Worried (pinched raised inner brows, tight mouth); Intense (sharp fixed stare, serious mouth); Synced (serene concentration, eyes bright and markings vivid).
Row 3: Amused (knowing half-smile); Smug (one raised brow, self-satisfied crooked grin); Curious (questioning head tilt, attentive eyes); Flustered (averted eyes, embarrassed uneven smile, subtle skin blush only).
Row 4: Tender (soft affectionate eyes and gentle closed smile); Determined (firm jaw and focused brows); Playful (one eye wink, broad mischievous grin); Special (joyful uninhibited laugh, eyes squeezed closed).
Do not rearrange or merge cells. No sweat drops, floating hearts, thought bubbles or decorative expression marks. Full square atlas 2048x2048 or largest native square.

Character: Old Tern, herd-reader of Lastlight, a new VERY OLD Kept woman, NOT any character in the references; only the art style and the sheet layout come from them. Small and bowed with age, seated and bundled in three layered hides (a pale shaggy fleece over a brown hide over a dark one), only her head and shoulders showing. Warm dun-brown fur gone silver-white at the muzzle and throat; a long grizzled brow ruff so long that it droops down over her LEFT eye in every cell; long silver cheek-whiskers braided into thin plaits, each plait tipped with small carved bone beads; bright, amused, very alive dark eyes in a deeply weathered face. A carved bone counting-stick, notched along its length, tucked through the hides across her chest. Unhurried, exact, teasing; she tells things once. Her most used faces are Amused (a slow sly half-smile, eyes crinkled), Neutral, Tender, Worried and Determined: make those clearly readable. Civilian clothing.
